decision_table.name: Determine_NE_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Nebraska state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus (considering PL 86-272 protections).

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in NE (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets NE economic nexus threshold (beyond PL 86-272 protection)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
NE filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in NE if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in NE - Employees working in NE - Tangible personal property located in NE - Real property located in NE
Nebraska imposes corporate income tax on any corporation doing business in the state, unless protected by Public Law 86-272 (for businesses solely soliciting orders for tangible personal property shipped from outside Nebraska).
Reference: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2701.13 (Nexus and doing business) Reference: Nebraska Department of Revenue Chapter 24 (Corporate Income Tax) Reference: Public Law 86-272 (Interstate commerce protection)

actions.action: // Economic nexus established (beyond PL 86-272) - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
NE filing required due to economic nexus (activities exceed PL 86-272 protections).
Economic nexus applies when a corporation has significant economic activity in Nebraska that exceeds the protections of Public Law 86-272. Unlike sales tax (which has a $100,000 threshold), income tax nexus depends on the nature and extent of business activities.
PL 86-272 protects businesses whose only activity is soliciting orders for tangible personal property approved and shipped from outside the state. Activities beyond mere solicitation create nexus for corporate income tax purposes.
Reference: Public Law 86-272 (Interstate commerce protection) Reference: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2701.13 (Doing business definition) Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018)

No NE nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in NE, or is protected by Public Law 86-272. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2701.13 (Nexus requirements) Reference: Public Law 86-272 (Interstate commerce protection)

decision_table.name: Calculate_NE_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate NE state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
NE state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
NE ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest or dividends from obligations of District of Columbia, other states, or their political subdivisions (except for regulated investment companies) - These are exempt at federal level or for other states but taxable to Nebraska
NE SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest or dividend income from U.S. government obligations and territories (Exempt from state tax per federal law, to extent includable in federal income) - Interest from Nebraska Build America Bonds (to extent includable federally) - Nebraska net operating loss deduction (subject to NE-specific limitations)
Expense adjustments: - Any amounts added/subtracted must be reduced by related expenses - Interest on debt to carry obligations is not deductible - Expenses in production of exempt income are not deductible
Reference: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2716 (Income tax adjustments) Reference: Nebraska Form 1120N Schedule I (Adjustments to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: Nebraska Department of Revenue Information Guide 8-646 (Interest/Dividend Taxability)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have NE nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_NE_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate NE state corporate income tax. Applies NE 5.20% flat rate (2025) to apportioned and adjusted taxable income. Rate will decrease to 4.55% (2026) and 3.99% (2027) under LB 754.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
NE state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to NE: × [NE apportionment percentage] 3. NE additions: + [Non-NE municipal interest, etc.] 4. NE subtractions: - [Federal interest, NE Build America Bonds, NE NOL, etc.] 5. NE taxable income: = [Result] 6. NE tax rate: × 5.20% (2025 rate) 7. NE income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. NE credits: - [Jobs, R&D, renewable energy, etc.] 9. NE tax liability: = [Final tax]
NE uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
NE tax rate schedule (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2734.02): - 2025: 5.20% flat rate - 2026: 4.55% flat rate - 2027+: 3.99% flat rate
Historical rates (pre-LB 754): - Before 2025: Two-tier system (5.58% on first $100K, 7.25% above)
NE provides various tax credits including: - Jobs creation credits - Research and development credits - Renewable energy credits - Beginning farmer tax credit - Nebraska advantage credits
Reference: Nebraska Form 1120N (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2734.02 (Tax rate of 5.20% for 2025) Reference: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2716 (Adjustments to federal income) Reference: Nebraska Department of Revenue Chapter 24 (Corporate Income Tax) Reference: LB 754 (2023) - Corporate tax reform and rate reduction schedule

No NE nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in NE, or is protected by Public Law 86-272. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2701.13 (Nexus requirements) Reference: Public Law 86-272 (Interstate commerce protection)

No NE taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has NE nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
NE net operating loss (NOL) rules: - NE follows federal NOL provisions with state-specific adjustments - NOL carryforward rules apply (subject to limitations) - State NOL must be computed separately from federal NOL - NOL limited based on Nebraska taxable income
Reference: Nebraska Form 1120N (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2716 (Adjustments including NOL) Reference: Nebraska Form 1120N Schedule II (Net Operating Loss Computation)
